assignments.reason: Memory (זכרון) is the faculty that preserves the imprint of the tzaddik's sekhel and neshamah in the student's mind. Its essential nature is the retention of the soul/intellect transmission — the very substance that Package 1 describes. Without זכרון, the engraved image of the tzaddik's face, intellect, and soul fades (line 6: 'שכחה משכחת הכל ממנו'). Memory belongs to the domain of soul and intellect because it is the vessel that holds them.

Reviewing 101 times is the act of the 'eved' (servant of God) — the one who embodies devotion to preserving the master's sekhel/neshamah. The Rebbe equates this practice with 'oved Elokim' (Hagigah 9b), one who serves God. Its essential nature is holy intellectual labor directed at retaining the soul/intellect transmission. It belongs to the same domain as נשמה and חכמה because it is the method by which the student secures the tzaddik's inner essence within himself.

Remembering what one receives from one's master is the actualized state of retaining the tzaddik's sekhel and neshamah. Its essential nature is identical to the core of Package 1: the student now holds within his da'at (mind) the intellect and soul of the sage. This is not merely a practical outcome but the very definition of successful soul/intellect transmission.

assignments.node_id: זוכה להיות כרבו, כי נזדמן לו דמות דיוקנו של רבו, וכאלו רבו אמרו אז כנ"ל, כי נחקק ונצטיר היטב בדעתו פנים ודמות רבו כדיו כתובה על הניר
assignments.reason: This node describes the ultimate fulfillment of the soul/intellect transmission: the student merits being like his master because the master's face (פנים), image (דמות דיוקן), and soul are fully engraved in his mind 'like ink on paper.' Its essential nature is the completed reception of the tzaddik's neshamah and sekhel — the perfected state of what Package 1 describes. The face, intellect, and soul of the tzaddik are all one substance (line 5: 'מקבל פניו ושכלו ונשמתו'), and this node represents their complete internalization.
